content.title: About
content.content: Lentil curry with rice is a fragrant Indian-inspired dish where red or green lentils are simmered in a spiced tomato‑coconut sauce and served over fluffy rice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lentils are one of the world’s oldest cultivated legumes, grown for over 8,000 years.
Traditional curry often uses garam masala, a blend of coriander, cumin, cardamom, and cloves.
Coconut milk softens the heat of the spices and adds a creamy texture.
The dish can be easily made vegan by using plant‑based oil instead of butter.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Lentils provide about 18 g of protein per 100 g, making them an excellent protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These micronutrients are essential for blood formation and anemia prevention, especially in women of child‑bearing age.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The combination of lentils and whole‑grain rice provides a steady release of energy.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Turmeric, cumin, and coriander are rich in polyphenols that combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lentils.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytates can reduce mineral absorption; soaking lentils before cooking helps mitigate this.

items.title: Watch sodium levels
items.content: If using pre‑made sauces, monitor salt content to avoid excess sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook lentils until partially tender, then simmer with tomato puree, coconut milk, spices, and a splash of water for 15‑20 minutes. Serve over boiled or steamed rice, garnished with fresh cilantro and lime wedges.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Freeze portions in freezer bags for up to 2 months. Reheat gently, adding a little water or broth to restore the creamy consistency.
